# Implementation overview

The public R interface connects genotype input, population objects, trait
simulation, prediction, and selection. The diagram groups these operations so
that the feedback from selection to the next generation remains visible.
Each box represents a subsystem, not a single function call.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Main workflow. Each box groups public operations; the tables below identify the implementing functions and languages."
flowchart TB
  input["Genotypes and founders"]
  pop["Population / haplotypes"]
  traits["Phenotype model"]
  expression["Expression model"]
  inspect["Inspect / export"]
  select["Predict / select"]
  cross["Mate / cross"]
  input --> pop
  input --> traits
  pop --> traits
  expression --> traits
  traits --> inspect
  traits --> select
  select --> cross
  cross --> pop
  classDef api fill:#e6f2f1,stroke:#24787b,color:#18373d;
  class input,pop,traits,expression,inspect,select,cross api;
```

## Where the first example runs

The public calls `simulate_phenotype()` and `additive()` build and realize a
`phenotype_sim`. Internal R functions sample causal markers, draw effects,
construct genetic values, scale components, and draw residuals. Inspection
functions expose the resulting values and metadata.

| Operation | Representative implementation |
|---|---|
| Normalize and validate inputs | `.normalize_geno()`, `.check_arch_args()` |
| Sample causal markers | `.draw_qtn()` |
| Construct effect series | `.effect_series()` |
| Assemble and scale genetic values | `.component_raw()`, `.genetic_matrix()` |
| Draw and scale residuals | `.draw_residual()`, `.seeded_residual()` |
| Assemble phenotype and diagnostics | `.realize_phenotype()`, `.variance_budget()` |

The [developer index](developer-index.qmd) supplies current source locations.

## Randomness and Rust

On the meiosis path, R draws the random quantities and passes them to Rust's
recombination implementation. QTN sampling and effect and residual draws also
stay in R. This boundary is part of the package's reproducibility contract.

The coalescent founder generator is an explicit exception: its Rust engine uses
a PRNG seeded through R. This is a separate path from the isqg parity-sensitive
meiosis implementation. Numericalization and stable hashing are deterministic
Rust operations. The source modules are `numeric.rs`, `meiosis.rs`, `genome.rs`,
`hash.rs`, and `coalescent.rs`.

| Implementation boundary | R interface or helper | Rust kernel |
|---|---|---|
| Genotype numericalization | `as_numeric()` and format handlers | `numericalize_core()` |
| Meiosis with R-supplied randomness | `.draw_meiosis()` and mating helpers | `meiosis_core()`, `mate_many_core()` |
| Stable identifiers | `.stable_key()` and related helpers | `stable_hash_core()` |
| Coalescent founders with seeded Rust randomness | `founders_coalescent()` | `coalescent_chromosome_core()` |

## Legacy and modern interfaces

`create_phenotypes()` retains its own legacy implementation. It is not a wrapper
around the composable grammar. Its examples and theory must therefore be checked
against the legacy source separately rather than inferred from modern examples.
